Elena Ruiz: Hey team — we're seeing inconsistent embedding sizes coming back from the embeddings endpoint depending on where we hit it. Hosted API returns vectors of length 1536, but our Private deployment (on-prem) returns 1024 and downstream similarity code is failing with "dimension mismatch". This started after we migrated the private cluster to the new infra image last week. Request id from a failing call: req_0a9b3c. Sample payload we use (python SDK):

Elena Ruiz: ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED", base_url="https://private.company.internal/v1")
vec = client.embeddings.create(model="redwood-embed-1", input="The quick brown fox")
print(len(vec.data[0].embedding))
```

Elena Ruiz: On hosted we do `curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":"The quick brown fox"}'` and it prints 1536. On private it prints 1024. Any idea what's going on? @John Rivera tagging support since this breaks prod similarity scoring :grimacing:

John Rivera: Thanks @Elena Ruiz — sorry you're hitting this. First quick q: can you paste the `model` string you pass to both hosted and private (exactly), and the response `model_id`/`model_version` fields if present in the JSON response? also send the raw response body (redact embeddings values if needed) and the `X-Request-Id` header from the private call (if different from req_0a9b3c).

Elena Ruiz: sure — hosted request body has `"model": "redwood-embed-1"`. Hosted response top-level shows `"model": "redwood-embed-1@v3"`. Private response that fails shows `"model": "redwood-embed-1@v1"` and `"embedding_dim": 1024` in the metadata. Private `X-Request-Id` is `req_0a9b3c` (same as I shared). Full (sanitized) response snippets: 

Elena Ruiz: ```json
// hosted response (trimmed)
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-1@v3",
  "data": [{"embedding": [ /* 1536 floats */ ]}],
  "usage": {"tokens": 7}
}

// private response (trimmed)
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-1@v1",
  "embedding_dim": 1024,
  "data": [{"embedding": [ /* 1024 floats */ ]}],
  "usage": {"tokens": 7}
}
```

John Rivera: Ok that already explains the mismatch — hosted is serving v3 while private is still on v1. Two follow-ups: (1) why private didn't pull v3 during the infra image upgrade; (2) why the `model` string didn't enforce parity. I'm escalating to eng infra and ml infra to confirm model mapping. @Marco Li can you check the private model registry mapping for their tenant and whether the deploy step pinned to v1?

Marco Li: looking. On our side the private control plane uses a mapping file that translates logical model name -> model artifact hash. For this customer the mapping file still points redwood-embed-1 -> sha256:abcd1234 (artifact v1). The canary/hosted mapping points to sha256:ff11ee22 (v3). It looks like the image upgrade applied runtime patches but did not refresh the mapping config from the control plane because their private install is cached (we allow offline mode). I can push an updated mapping, but first let's confirm compatibility and whether v3 has a different embed head.

Priya Shah: v3 definitely has a different projection head and new embedding_dim=1536 — it's an intentional change to improve semantic capacity. That's why you see 1536 vs 1024. Batching or request size won't change dimension size — it's model-specific. The fix options: (A) update the private mapping to point to v3 so both match, (B) re-run offline re-embedding of your dataset and change downstream logic to expect 1536, or (C) run a migration shim that expands/downsamples vectors (bad for accuracy). Recommendation: sync to v3.

Elena Ruiz: If we sync to v3, will we be charged differently? We noticed a billing spike last month and worried a model change will increase cost. Also will latency change? We have strict SLA.

BillingBot: Note: model v3 has 50% higher per-embedding unit cost in hosted pricing table. If the private cluster is under a reserved plan, cost depends on reserved slot usage; we'll need to run a delta estimate for Elena's monthly volume. @Elena Ruiz please share monthly embedding calls (approx) and whether private is under a reserved contract.

Elena Ruiz: We're at ~1.2M embeddings/mo. Private is on a Dedicated reserved contract.

Marco Li: latency wise v3 median is +8ms on GPU for the same sequence length. Throughput might be slightly lower if you keep same batch sizing; we should run a perf sweep. For private we can control quantization/opt level. If cost is a concern we can recommend `quantize=int8` variant which preserves dim=1536 but reduces cost/throughput impact.

John Rivera: Back to reproducing: @Elena Ruiz can you run these two quick checks and paste outputs? 1) GET model metadata from both endpoints: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/redwood-embed-1/metadata` and `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://private.company.internal/v1/models/redwood-embed-1/metadata`. 2) Run tokenization check on a canonical string to ensure tokenizers align (just in case): `python -c "from redwood.tokenizer import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer.for_model('redwood-embed-1').encode('The quick brown fox'))"`

Elena Ruiz: ran both, outputs below. Hosted metadata: `{"model":"redwood-embed-1@v3","embedding_dim":1536,"artifact":"ff11ee22"}`. Private metadata: `{"model":"redwood-embed-1@v1","embedding_dim":1024,"artifact":"abcd1234"}`. Tokenizer encodes returned identical token sequences.

Priya Shah: tokenizers matching is expected; this is purely a model head change. So next steps: Marco to push mapping update to private, support to coordinate a maintenance window. Also we should provide a temporary workaround: the client can request a specific model variant via model alias `redwood-embed-1@v3` if the private control plane makes v3 available. Try passing `model: "redwood-embed-1@v3"` to your private endpoint — if it errors it means artifact not present.

Elena Ruiz: tried `model: "redwood-embed-1@v3"` on private and got 404: `artifact not found`. So artifact v3 isn't on the private nodes.

Marco Li: confirming — artifact v3 isn't in the customer's offline artifact store. I can push the artifact (requires ~2GB transfer) and update mapping. We should schedule because private nodes will restart the model runtime for the new artifact. Proposed maintenance window: tonight 02:00-02:30 UTC.

Elena Ruiz: maintenance window works. Can you estimate risk? Any chance of losing data or changing behavior other than embedding dim?

Priya Shah: low risk for data loss — only the model artifact changes. Model outputs will change as embeddings are different; downstream similarity will need reindexing or re-embedding for parity. If you don't want to re-embed, we could instead re-run your similarity service to down-project v3->1024 but that's lossy. Best is to update model and re-embed or roll back hosted to v1 (not recommended).

John Rivera: I've opened an internal ticket INC-12345 and marked it P1 for customer impact. Elena I'll coordinate post-maintenance validation — we'll provide a small test harness you can run to verify dims/values.

Elena Ruiz: thanks. Also one more weirdness: when we hit the private endpoint with batching enabled (`batch_size=64`) we're seeing occasional 500 errors with body `"runtime: embedding head mismatch"` — could that be because some nodes have v1 and some v3 causing mixed-shard results?

Marco Li: yes that's a good catch — if some nodes have v1 and some v3, a batch touching both could fail when runtime aggregates shapes. That's likely what caused the 500. After mapping update we'll ensure all nodes get artifact v3 before re-enabling large batch sizes. In the interim, set `batch_size=1` or smaller to avoid cross-shard mixing.

Elena Ruiz: great, we'll set `batch_size=1` as workaround. Please also share the validation script.

John Rivera: attaching simple validation harness (run on your side after maintenance):

John Rivera: ```bash
# validation.sh
set -e
API=$1
KEY=$2
for s in "The quick brown fox" "lorem ipsum dolor sit amet" "redwood inference test"; do
  resp=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d "{\\\"model\\\":\\\"redwood-embed-1@v3\\\",\\\"input\\\":\\\"$s\\\"}" $API/v1/embeddings)
  dim=$(echo "$resp" | jq '.data[0].embedding | length')
  echo "$s -> dim=$dim"
done
```

John Rivera: After maintenance I'll also provide a perf matrix for v1 vs v3 on your private hardware so you can decide quantization/cost tradeoffs.

Elena Ruiz: Perfect. Thanks all. I'll keep this thread updated post-maintenance.

Marco Li: Deploy completed on all nodes at 2025-12-05T02:12:40Z, mapping updated to point redwood-embed-1 -> ff11ee22.

Elena Ruiz: post-deploy check — ran John's validation, all three test strings returned `dim=1536`. No 500s when running `batch_size=16` test. Thank you.

John Rivera: closing the loop: INC-12345 -> Resolved (model parity achieved). Reindexing note: please file separate ticket if you want Redwood to assist with re-embedding or provide a migration plan for your stored vectors.

Elena Ruiz: filed a follow-up ticket for re-embedding assistance. Appreciate the quick turnaround :tada:
